title: David and Goliath
lead: The young shepherd David's victory with a sling over the Philistine champion of Gath in the Valley of Elah (1 Samuel 17), the Bible's best-known underdog story. Its text survives in a long Hebrew form and a much shorter Greek one, and 2 Samuel 21:19 credits Goliath's death to a man named Elhanan.

sections.b: Goliath of Gath challenges Israel for forty days until David kills him with a sling stone and cuts off his head with the giant's own sword (1 Samuel 17). The sword is later kept at Nob, wrapped behind the ephod, and given to David as he flees (1 Samuel 21:9; 1 Samuel 22:10). A list of David's heroes says that "Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite" killed "Goliath the Gittite," whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam (2 Samuel 21:19), while Chronicles says Elhanan killed "Lahmi the brother of Goliath" (1 Chronicles 20:5). Psalm 144 carries the Greek heading "against Goliath," and the Greek Psalm 151 has David remember cutting off the giant's head.
